clue.text: Winning easily, start to grow more intense

definitions.meaning: a side comfortably ahead in a match is said to be well in front
as feelings or tears do when they rise and swell

explanation.surface: A competitor coasting to victory feels their excitement build.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: being comfortably ahead, and emotions rising to the surface.

clue.text: In France good noise comes with good rapport

parts.note: the French word for good is bon
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A pleasant French sound goes along with friendly relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonding is the forming of a close relationship, which is a rapport between people.

clue.text: Loss of employment is hard — party must be held

indicators.note: one piece is held by the other, so the party word sits inside the word for hard

parts.note: severe means hard or harsh
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African political party

explanation.surface: Being sacked is tough, so throw a farewell party.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANC is South Africa's African National Congress; 'must be held' signals that the hard word holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance is the ending of a person's job contract, often with a payout.

clue.text: Greek character has briefly purloined weapon

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: a word said briefly loses its final letter, here the last of the word for purloined

parts.note: purloined means stole

explanation.surface: A Greek has stolen a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a type of weapon.

clue.text: Bikes in next to no time sped furiously

parts.note: a mo is a moment, almost no time at all

indicators.note: doing something furiously throws it about wildly, so the letters of sped are jumbled

explanation.surface: Motorbikes raced off at speed in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Small motorised two-wheelers are a kind of bike.

clue.text: Dampness damaged tourism — last thing Margate needs

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of tourism are rearranged
the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Wet weather has hurt seaside visitor numbers, the last thing the Kent resort of Margate wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TOURISM to MOISTUR; 'last thing' gives E from Margate, a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Moisture is water present in small amounts, which is what dampness consists of.

clue.text: Dance has the old man taking front position

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
the van is the leading position, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Dad takes the lead on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavan is a stately court dance of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: I do a turn, being funny for a time

indicators.note: something being funny is odd or peculiar, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian takes the stage to perform a comic routine for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being funny' rearranges I DO A TURN; 'a turn' suggests a comedy act.
explanation.definitionFit: A duration is a length or period of time.

clue.text: Secret English drunkard, top woman in charge

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A hidden English drinker turns out to be the woman running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is known only to an inner few, so it is in effect private or hidden.

clue.text: Old TV comic Phil gets more than one second prize

definitions.meaning: Phil ..., the American comedian who played Sergeant Bilko
second place wins a silver medal, so several such awards

explanation.surface: A veteran comedian picks up several runner-up awards.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Bilko star, and the plural of the medal given to runners-up.

clue.text: Stay for a while in porter's house?

definitions.meaning: to live somewhere temporarily as a guest or tenant
a college or estate porter works from a small gatehouse

explanation.surface: An invitation to stop over at the doorkeeper's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for staying as a lodger, and the small building by an entrance gate where a porter sits.

clue.text: Old boy in state that's unstable and unlikely to change

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: an unstable mix does not hold its form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former pupil in a shaky country is set in his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the fodder that 'that's unstable' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person stubbornly refuses to alter their opinion.

clue.text: Bill's little companion in Scottish mountain

definitions.meaning: Bill and ... were the Flowerpot Men of British children's television
in Scotland a ... is a mountain peak, as in ... Nevis

explanation.surface: A friend of Bill's is up a Highland peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill and Ben were a pair of puppets on an old BBC children's show, and Scots call a mountain a ben.

clue.text: Star writer with story about origin of cricket

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the story word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A star author tells a tale about how cricket began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' gives C, which 'about' places inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star used as a magic symbol.

clue.text: Animal that surprises me has rushed around

indicators.note: the word for rushed goes around the exclamation

parts.note: ran means rushed
coo is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A startled onlooker watches a creature dashing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A racoon is a North American mammal with a masked face.

clue.text: Opposing inauthentic sort of singing in church

parts.note: anti means against or opposing
phony means fake

explanation.surface: A critic objects to the fake choir performance at a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is responsive chanting in which two choirs or groups alternate verses.

clue.text: Vessels — they glide along?

definitions.meaning: ships trading along a coastline from port to port
those who move easily without effort, or sledges and toboggans that freewheel

explanation.surface: A question whether ships move smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal trading ships, and anyone or anything that freewheels without effort.

clue.text: Method of payment on doorstep for fish

definitions.meaning: cash on delivery, paying when goods arrive at the door
a common food fish of northern seas

explanation.surface: Paying for a fish delivery when it reaches the door.
explanation.definitionFit: An initialism for paying on delivery, and a familiar white fish.

clue.text: Spectator as a weekly publication

definitions.meaning: an onlooker who watches events
a British Sunday newspaper, the oldest in the world

explanation.surface: A British magazine described as a weekly periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading The Spectator, itself a British weekly magazine, but the word here means an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches, and the title of a long-running British Sunday paper.

clue.text: Information supplied by agent

indicators.note: the letters are provided from inside the following word

explanation.surface: A spy hands over intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British slang for facts or information.

clue.text: Fairy in a Shakespeare play, fine material

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairy attendants in A Midsummer Night's Dream
the delicate silk threads a spider spins

explanation.surface: A sprite on stage wears a costume of delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A named fairy in a Shakespeare comedy, and the gauzy strands spun by spiders.

clue.text: One watches, missing odd bits

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone observing has lost some odd pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a playing card or die face worth one.

clue.text: Loud goings-on in party

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
action means activity or happenings

explanation.surface: Raucous behaviour at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group within a larger party.

clue.text: Like many a Catholic priest in church, albeit naughty

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is unruly, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A priest misbehaving in church despite his vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Catholic clergy are bound to remain unmarried and abstain from sex.

clue.text: Everything one has in car

definitions.meaning: all of a person's property and possessions, especially at death
a British name for a station wagon with a large rear load space

explanation.surface: Someone's entire wealth is tied up in their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's whole property, and the British term for a station wagon.

clue.text: Making appearance outside house, city journalist returned

indicators.note: the first pieces appear on the outside of the house abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaperman showing up outside a home comes back to the City.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London; 'Making appearance outside' has city and journalist wrap the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound that echoes comes back off a surface, so it is returned.

clue.text: One has unexpected closeness, no win ultimately, having two sides equal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out differently, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of win is taken

explanation.surface: A competitor is caught off guard by a tight contest that ends without a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes N, the last letter of win ('ultimately'); 'unexpected' rearranges what is left of CLOSENESS into SOSCELES.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle is one with a pair of equal-length sides.

clue.text: Mythical being, after last day of week, starts to yawn and relax

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A creature of legend yawns and unwinds when the weekend comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a goat-like woodland deity in Greek myth.

clue.text: Problem for film director

definitions.meaning: a snag or setback
the nickname of Alfred Hitchcock

explanation.surface: A movie director runs into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or temporary difficulty, and the shortened name by which Alfred Hitchcock was known.

clue.text: Female dumping male by street, I have to be merry

indicators.note: the female word drops the male word from inside itself

parts.note: I've contracts I have

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her man on the street and decides to cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping' removes MALE from FEMALE, leaving FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive mood is cheerful and celebratory.

clue.text: Vehicle taking Laurel and Bob maybe

parts.note: Stan Laurel, of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
Bob Hope, the comedian, as one example of a Bob

explanation.surface: A film comedy pairing two famous comics as co-stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' in the surface suggests a star vehicle, a film built around its leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage, a kind of conveyance.

clue.text: Type of moneylender certain to be found in old city

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed inside the city name

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A particular lender is sure to be found in an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, a predatory kind of lender.
